d: The finger of peritoneum that leads the testis through the inguinal canal during descent; its closed lower end becomes the tunica vaginalis, and a patent processus allows a communicating hydrocele or an indirect hernia.
Malignant germ cells still confined within the seminiferous tubules; it is the precursor of most postpubertal testicular germ cell tumors, including seminoma and embryonal carcinoma.
An abnormally high attachment of the tunica vaginalis that leaves the testis hanging free, like the clapper inside a bell, so it can rotate and twist the spermatic cord; it is usually bilateral.
Relief of scrotal pain when the testis is lifted; it favors epididymitis, because elevation eases traction on the inflamed epididymis, and it is absent in testicular torsion.
A glomerulus-like structure of tumor cells wrapped around a central blood vessel inside a small space; it is the histologic hallmark of yolk sac tumor.
Rod-shaped eosinophilic inclusions in the cytoplasm of Leydig cells; they help identify a Leydig cell tumor, which makes androgens or estrogens rather than AFP or hCG.
